newsitem.title: UK: Grain markets have strong upside potential - Goldman.
newsitem.headline: Grain markets have strong upside potential - Goldman.

text.p: Low stocks, a continuing uptrend in global demand and a shortage of new arable land mean world wheat, corn and soybean markets have potential rise again, said Marklin Williams, head of grain trading at Goldman, Sachs & Co.
U.S. soybean crops additionally face the threat of a late frost, let alone an early or normal frost, he added.
Corn stocks could be tight again next year and "prices still have significant potential to improve over the next year," Williams told Goldman, Sachs' annual commodity conference here.

If U.S. feed use of wheat turns out to be underestimated -- new estimates are due next week -- then Williams said prices could turn up and make new highs and this could be the powder keg for the whole grain sector.
Williams, a Goldman's vice president, said stocks-to-usage ratios were critically low for wheat, corn and soybeans.
Economists had underestimated demand in Asia outside Japan where feed usage had risen reflecting strong meat demand, Williams said.
